name: Enable weekly SSD trim
description: Enable fstrim.timer so unused blocks on SSDs and thin volumes are discarded weekly.

name: Lower swap tendency
description: Set vm.swappiness to 10 so the kernel keeps file cache longer before swapping. Undo restores the previous runtime value.
apply:
set -eu
prevfile=/etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-swappiness.conf.prev
if [ ! -f "$prevfile" ]; then
    old=$(sysctl -n vm.swappiness)
    printf '%s\n' "$old" > "$prevfile"
fi
printf '%s\n' 'vm.swappiness=10' > /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-swappiness.conf
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=10
undo:
set -eu
prevfile=/etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-swappiness.conf.prev
if [ -f "$prevfile" ]; then old=$(cat "$prevfile"); else old=60; fi
if [ -z "$old" ]; then old=60; fi
case $old in
    *[!0-9A-Za-z._-]*) old=60 ;;
esac
rm -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-swappiness.conf "$prevfile"
sysctl -w vm.swappiness="$old"

name: Compressed RAM swap
description: Write a zram-generator config for a zstd zram device of half of RAM, capped at 4 GiB, and start it. Requires zram-generator (Debian package systemd-zram-generator). An existing config is backed up first. Undo stops that device and restores the backup, or deletes the file if this tweak created it.
apply:
set -eu
conf=/etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf
bak=/etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf.tuxutil.bak
if [ -f "$conf" ] && [ ! -f "$bak" ]; then cp "$conf" "$bak"; fi
printf '%s\n' '[zram0]' 'zram-size = min(ram / 2, 4096)' 'compression-algorithm = zstd' 'swap-priority = 100' > "$conf"
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl start systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service
undo:
set -eu
conf=/etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf
bak=/etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf.tuxutil.bak
systemctl stop systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service || true
if [ -f "$bak" ]; then
    cp "$bak" "$conf"
    rm -f "$bak"
else
    rm -f "$conf"
fi
systemctl daemon-reload

name: Do not wait for NetworkManager at boot
description: Disable NetworkManager-wait-online.service so boot does not sit there until the network is online. Networking itself still starts.

name: Enable UFW
description: Turn on UFW with incoming traffic denied, outgoing traffic allowed, and OpenSSH allowed. Other inbound services stop answering until you allow them.

name: Enable firewalld
description: Enable firewalld. The default public zone allows SSH and DHCPv6 client and blocks other inbound traffic.

name: DNS over TLS
description: Point systemd-resolved at Cloudflare over TLS and restart it. Name lookup fails if the network blocks port 853. Undo deletes the drop-in and restarts resolved.
apply:
set -eu
mkdir -p /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d
printf '%s\n' '[Resolve]' 'DNS=1.1.1.1#cloudflare-dns.com 1.0.0.1#cloudflare-dns.com' 'DNSOverTLS=yes' 'DNSSEC=allow-downgrade' > /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/99-tuxutil-dot.conf
systemctl restart systemd-resolved.service

name: Enable Bluetooth
description: Enable and start bluetooth.service. The bluez package has to be installed already.

name: Enable printing
description: Enable and start cups.service. The cups package has to be installed already.

name: Pacman parallel downloads
description: Set ParallelDownloads to 5 in /etc/pacman.conf. The commented default downloads one package at a time. The original file is copied to /etc/pacman.conf.tuxutil-parallel.bak and undo restores it.
apply:
set -eu
src=/etc/pacman.conf
bak=/etc/pacman.conf.tuxutil-parallel.bak
if [ ! -f "$bak" ]; then cp "$src" "$bak"; fi
if grep -q '^ParallelDownloads' "$src"; then
    sed -i 's/^ParallelDownloads.*/ParallelDownloads = 5/' "$src"
elif grep -q '^#ParallelDownloads' "$src"; then
    sed -i 's/^#ParallelDownloads.*/ParallelDownloads = 5/' "$src"
else
    printf '\n%s\n' 'ParallelDownloads = 5' >> "$src"
fi

name: Enable the multilib repository
description: Uncomment the [multilib] section in /etc/pacman.conf so 32-bit libraries can be installed. Undo restores the backup. Run pacman -Sy yourself afterwards; this tweak does not refresh the databases.
apply:
set -eu
src=/etc/pacman.conf
bak=/etc/pacman.conf.tuxutil-multilib.bak
if [ ! -f "$bak" ]; then cp "$src" "$bak"; fi
sed -i '/^#\[multilib\]$/{s/^#//;n;s/^#Include/Include/}' "$src"

name: APT download settings
description: Drop in apt settings that keep a small pipeline of downloads, skip translation indexes, and retry three times. Recommended packages stay enabled.

name: DNF parallel downloads
description: Set max_parallel_downloads=10 in /etc/dnf/dnf.conf, which both DNF 4 and DNF 5 read. Undo restores the backup. The value stays under DNF5's limit of 20.
apply:
set -eu
src=/etc/dnf/dnf.conf
bak=/etc/dnf/dnf.conf.tuxutil.bak
if [ ! -f "$bak" ]; then cp "$src" "$bak"; fi
if grep -q '^max_parallel_downloads=' "$src"; then
    sed -i 's/^max_parallel_downloads=.*/max_parallel_downloads=10/' "$src"
else
    printf '\n%s\n' 'max_parallel_downloads=10' >> "$src"
fi

name: Zypper parallel downloads
description: Set download.max_concurrent_connections to 8 via /etc/zypp/zypp.conf.d. Current Tumbleweed and recent Leap read that directory. Undo deletes the drop-in.

name: Add the Flathub remote
description: Add the system Flathub remote if it is missing, and remember that this tweak added it. Undo removes the remote only in that case, and leaves a remote that was already there.
apply:
set -eu
if flatpak remotes --system | awk '{print $1}' | grep -qx flathub; then
    exit 0
fi
flatpak remote-add --system --if-not-exists flathub https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo
mkdir -p /etc/tuxutil
touch /etc/tuxutil/flathub-added
undo:
set -eu
if [ -f /etc/tuxutil/flathub-added ]; then
    flatpak remote-delete --system flathub
    rm -f /etc/tuxutil/flathub-added
fi

name: Raise vm.max_map_count
description: Set vm.max_map_count to 1048576, which Steam, Proton, and some games need. Undo restores the previous runtime value (the kernel default is 65530).
apply:
set -eu
prevfile=/etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-max-map-count.conf.prev
if [ ! -f "$prevfile" ]; then
    old=$(sysctl -n vm.max_map_count)
    printf '%s\n' "$old" > "$prevfile"
fi
printf '%s\n' 'vm.max_map_count=1048576' > /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-max-map-count.conf
sysctl -w vm.max_map_count=1048576
undo:
set -eu
prevfile=/etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-max-map-count.conf.prev
if [ -f "$prevfile" ]; then old=$(cat "$prevfile"); else old=65530; fi
if [ -z "$old" ]; then old=65530; fi
case $old in
    *[!0-9A-Za-z._-]*) old=65530 ;;
esac
rm -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-max-map-count.conf "$prevfile"
sysctl -w vm.max_map_count="$old"

name: Cap the journal size
description: Limit the persistent journal to 200M via a journald drop-in and restart systemd-journald. Undo deletes the drop-in and restarts it.
apply:
set -eu
mkdir -p /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d
printf '%s\n' '[Journal]' 'SystemMaxUse=200M' > /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/99-tuxutil.conf
systemctl restart systemd-journald.service

name: Opt out of popularity-contest
description: Set PARTICIPATE="no" in /etc/popularity-contest.conf so the Debian package survey does not run. An existing file is backed up first; undo restores it or deletes a file this tweak created.
apply:
set -eu
conf=/etc/popularity-contest.conf
bak=/etc/popularity-contest.conf.tuxutil.bak
if [ -f "$conf" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$bak" ]; then cp "$conf" "$bak"; fi
    if grep -q '^PARTICIPATE=' "$conf"; then
        sed -i 's/^PARTICIPATE=.*/PARTICIPATE="no"/' "$conf"
    else
        printf '\n%s\n' 'PARTICIPATE="no"' >> "$conf"
    fi
else
    printf '%s\n' 'PARTICIPATE="no"' > "$conf"
fi
undo:
set -eu
conf=/etc/popularity-contest.conf
bak=/etc/popularity-contest.conf.tuxutil.bak
if [ -f "$bak" ]; then
    cp "$bak" "$conf"
    rm -f "$bak"
else
    rm -f "$conf"
fi

name: Opt out of ubuntu-report
description: Run ubuntu-report -f send no for the current user. That stores an opt-out and sends Canonical a one-time opt-out ping, not a hardware report. It does not cover other accounts. Undo deletes that user's ubuntu-report cache.

name: Disable whoopsie error reports
description: Disable Ubuntu's whoopsie service, which uploads crash reports. Undo enables it again. The unit has to exist.

name: Enable network time
description: Enable systemd-timesyncd. If chrony or ntpd already owns NTP, systemd refuses to run both and this command fails.

name: TCP BBR congestion control
description: Use the BBR congestion control with the fq queueing discipline. Undo restores the previous runtime values (commonly cubic and fq_codel).
apply:
set -eu
conf=/etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-bbr.conf
if [ ! -f "$conf.qdisc.prev" ]; then sysctl -n net.core.default_qdisc > "$conf.qdisc.prev"; fi
if [ ! -f "$conf.cc.prev" ]; then sysctl -n net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control > "$conf.cc.prev"; fi
printf '%s\n' 'net.core.default_qdisc=fq' 'net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control=bbr' > "$conf"
sysctl -w net.core.default_qdisc=fq
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control=bbr
undo:
set -eu
conf=/etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-bbr.conf
qdisc=fq_codel
cc=cubic
if [ -f "$conf.qdisc.prev" ]; then qdisc=$(cat "$conf.qdisc.prev"); fi
if [ -f "$conf.cc.prev" ]; then cc=$(cat "$conf.cc.prev"); fi
case $qdisc in *[!0-9A-Za-z._-]*) qdisc=fq_codel ;; esac
case $cc in *[!0-9A-Za-z._-]*) cc=cubic ;; esac
rm -f "$conf" "$conf.qdisc.prev" "$conf.cc.prev"
sysctl -w net.core.default_qdisc="$qdisc"
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control="$cc"

name: Raise inotify watch limit
description: Set fs.inotify.max_user_watches to 524288 so large projects and file indexers do not run out of watches. Undo restores the previous runtime value.
apply:
set -eu
prevfile=/etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-inotify-watches.conf.prev
if [ ! -f "$prevfile" ]; then
    old=$(sysctl -n fs.inotify.max_user_watches)
    printf '%s\n' "$old" > "$prevfile"
fi
printf '%s\n' 'fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288' > /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-inotify-watches.conf
sysctl -w fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288
undo:
set -eu
prevfile=/etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-inotify-watches.conf.prev
if [ -f "$prevfile" ]; then old=$(cat "$prevfile"); else old=8192; fi
if [ -z "$old" ]; then old=8192; fi
case $old in
    *[!0-9A-Za-z._-]*) old=8192 ;;
esac
rm -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-inotify-watches.conf "$prevfile"
sysctl -w fs.inotify.max_user_watches="$old"

name: Raise open-file limit
description: Allow 524288 open files per login via /etc/security/limits.d. Already-open sessions keep the old limit until the next login. Undo deletes the drop-in.
apply:
set -eu
mkdir -p /etc/security/limits.d
printf '%s\n' '* soft nofile 524288' '* hard nofile 524288' > /etc/security/limits.d/99-tuxutil.conf

name: Do not store core dumps
description: Tell systemd-coredump to discard crash dumps instead of writing them under /var/lib/systemd/coredump. Undo deletes the drop-in. This does not change SELinux or AppArmor.

name: Automatic security upgrades
description: Enable APT's periodic unattended upgrades. Nothing is installed until the unattended-upgrades package is present; once it is, security updates install on their own.

name: Enable dnf-automatic
description: Enable dnf-automatic.timer from the dnf-automatic package. Whether updates are only downloaded or also installed depends on the existing /etc/dnf/automatic.conf.

name: Disable remote printer discovery
description: Disable cups-browsed, which discovers printers on the network and has a history of serious bugs. Local CUPS printing stays available. Undo enables the service again.

name: Clean the pacman cache weekly
description: Enable paccache.timer from pacman-contrib so old package versions are removed from the cache. The package has to be installed already.

name: Parallel makepkg builds
description: Set MAKEFLAGS="-j$(nproc)" in /etc/makepkg.conf so package builds use every core. Undo restores the backup.
apply:
set -eu
src=/etc/makepkg.conf
bak=/etc/makepkg.conf.tuxutil.bak
if [ ! -f "$bak" ]; then cp "$src" "$bak"; fi
if grep -q '^MAKEFLAGS=' "$src"; then
    sed -i 's|^MAKEFLAGS=.*|MAKEFLAGS="-j$(nproc)"|' "$src"
elif grep -q '^#MAKEFLAGS=' "$src"; then
    sed -i 's|^#MAKEFLAGS=.*|MAKEFLAGS="-j$(nproc)"|' "$src"
else
    printf '\n%s\n' 'MAKEFLAGS="-j$(nproc)"' >> "$src"
fi

name: Keep filesystem cache longer
description: Set vm.vfs_cache_pressure to 50 so directory and inode caches are reclaimed more slowly. Undo restores the previous runtime value (the kernel default is 100).
apply:
set -eu
prevfile=/etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-vfs-cache-pressure.conf.prev
if [ ! -f "$prevfile" ]; then
    old=$(sysctl -n vm.vfs_cache_pressure)
    printf '%s\n' "$old" > "$prevfile"
fi
printf '%s\n' 'vm.vfs_cache_pressure=50' > /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-vfs-cache-pressure.conf
sysctl -w vm.vfs_cache_pressure=50
undo:
set -eu
prevfile=/etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-vfs-cache-pressure.conf.prev
if [ -f "$prevfile" ]; then old=$(cat "$prevfile"); else old=100; fi
if [ -z "$old" ]; then old=100; fi
case $old in
    *[!0-9A-Za-z._-]*) old=100 ;;
esac
rm -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxutil-vfs-cache-pressure.conf "$prevfile"
sysctl -w vm.vfs_cache_pressure="$old"

name: Enable systemd-oomd
description: Enable systemd-oomd, which can kill processes when memory or swap is nearly full. Undo disables it.
